brief: A tool rack that hangs on a wall from keyhole hangers, with hooks for small hand tools.

requirements.evidence: Two single-storey keyhole hangers (accessory:0#0,0#0 and accessory:2#0,0#0) on face slot 0 of the bottom and top cells. Same face, so they sit in one plane against the wall, on two screws one above the other.
A column of three cells (piece 0,0,0 / 0,0,1 / 0,0,2) joined by two snaps. Slot 0 is the side that goes against the wall.

Five hook plates with two hooks each, so 10 hooks: slot 3, the face opposite the wall, on all three levels (accessory:0#0,0#3, 1#0,0#3, 2#0,0#3), plus the two angled front faces of the middle cell (accessory:1#0,0#2, 1#0,0#4).
check_build: ok, meshClash clear. The only note is an info item that 11 faces could take caps, which is optional.

finish.summary: Wall tool rack: a column of three cells hung on two keyhole hangers at the back, with five hook plates (10 hooks) on the front faces. 12 parts. It passes the checks with meshes clear. No load rating is claimed.

lines.label: M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
